objective: Decide independently whether GB-H1 (save migration), GB-H2 (post-boot fault recovery) and GB-TOUCH-SMOKE (visible touch controls) may move from under_review to verified, or whether any of the three is an implementation that its own test cannot falsify.
required_inputs: A disposable copy of the repository at the reviewed hashes
Playwright Chromium (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH as configured in this environment)
docs/DONE.md B2, B5, C5, D6 as the only acceptance authority
required_checks: Run npm run test:save, npm run test:faults and npm run test:touch in the disposable copy and confirm the reported counts.

Confirm each runner can fail: pass --force-failure to tools/fault_recovery.mjs and tools/touch_smoke.mjs and confirm a nonzero exit, and confirm every negative control in tools/save_migration.mjs is rejected by at least one check.

R-08 test: for each of the three runners, decide whether it executes the verb it claims. Specifically — does the save suite load through the production Storage.load path rather than calling migrateSave directly; does the fault probe cause real uncaught errors and rejections rather than calling the handler; does the touch probe reach the game through dispatched touch points rather than through input.setVirtual.

Attack the migration layer: a save at the current version, a legacy-key save, a newer-version save, a corrupt blob, a save with a non-integer version, a rescue slot that already holds something, and a private-browsing localStorage that throws on every write.
Attack the fault escalation rule: find a fault sequence that leaves a player with a stopped picture and no panel, or one that puts the panel in front of a player whose game is still running.

Check that the touch measurements are read from rendered geometry rather than from CSS the probe itself asserts, and that the run would fail if a control were moved off-screen, shrunk below 44px or overlapped.
Confirm no claim in docs/STATE.md, docs/bible.md or README.md added by this round asserts real-device behaviour, full Gate B, or a multi-step migration chain.
acceptance_criteria: A save written by the published v1 build loads, with flags, inventory, capabilities, quests, journal, chapter, play time and the world envelope intact.
A save this build cannot read is never destroyed and never silently overwritten by the autosave that follows, and the player is told in their own language.
An uncaught error or rejected promise after boot saves the game and reaches the player; a fault that leaves the frame counter stopped reaches the recovery panel; a single survivable fault does not.
Every visible control at 667x375 is at least 44 CSS px, on screen, non-overlapping and reachable by a dispatched touch, and the dead space between controls presses nothing.
Each runner exits nonzero when its subject is broken.
decision_rule: PASS a task only if its required checks complete with no unresolved high-severity finding in that task's scope. The three are judged separately: one may pass while another fails. Otherwise FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE for that task.
constraints: Do not use implementer prose, this handoff's summaries or README.md as evidence; read the source and run the build.
Do not alter shared product code, tests, state, evidence or prior reviews. The only permitted shared edit is the expected output review.
Do not approve B1 or any real-device claim, full Gate B, C1, D3, performance, play feel or release.
Run adversarial mutations only in a disposable copy.
known_risks: The migration chain has exactly one production step (v1 -> v2), so a two-or-more-step chain is unexercised by production data.

Chromium under SwiftShader runs the loop at a few frames a second; the fault and touch probes keep the page busy deliberately, and a reviewer should check that this does not mask a timing-dependent defect.
Emulated touch is not a thumb on glass (blocker B1).

Changing SAVE_KEY moves where a published player's save lives. The legacy key is read and then removed once the migrated copy is written; a reviewer should look for a sequence in which both copies can be lost.
invariants: A save that cannot be read is copied aside before anything can overwrite it, and the first rescued copy is never replaced.
A migration step must not mutate its input and must advance the version by exactly one.
The recovery panel is shown for a fault the game did not survive, not for every fault.
rollback_instructions: Revert src/game/state.js, src/main.js, public/index.html and src/content/locale/ja/ui.js; drop the three runners, the fixture and the three package scripts; restore state to revision 2026-08-01.1. A player who has already loaded the new build has their save at cinderline.save; reverting alone will not move it back, so a revert must also restore the legacy key or accept that those saves become the rescued copy.
